deep.reconstruction:
Context. This sheet (marked 'III') is a draft of the Dirichlet-principle argument in Riemann's 1851 Inaugural Dissertation (§§16–18). The next page states the conclusion: the minimising u satisfies Δu = 0 in every piece of the surface, plus a weak condition at the discontinuity curves. The strip is cut off at the left margin, so the stray marks there ('=0,', dashes, single letters) are line ends of a lost left half. In the dissertation the setting is as follows. T is a (possibly multi-sheeted) surface and β is a given function. u = α + λ ranges over functions with prescribed boundary values. The functional is Ω(u) = ∫∫_T [(u_x − β_y)^2 + (u_y + β_x)^2] dT.

(1) Uniqueness of the minimum value (faint pencil, top). Paraphrase: for these functions one obtains the same Ω. 𝔘 cannot be < U_1, and likewise U_1 cannot be < 𝔘; hence 𝔘 = U_1. Two candidate minima (lower bounds) of Ω over the admissible class must coincide, since neither can be strictly smaller than the other.

(2) First variation. Replace u by u + h u', where u' vanishes on the outer boundary ('u' = 0'). Then
Ω(u + h u') = Ω(u) + 2h ∫∫[(u_x − β_y) u'_x + (u_y + β_x) u'_y] dT + h^2 ∫∫(u'_x^2 + u'_y^2) dT.
The page writes the linear coefficient explicitly:
N := ∫[(u_x − β_y) u'_x + (u_y + β_x) u'_y] dT.
Riemann notes that the integrand involves only the two quantities u_x − β_y and u_y + β_x. These must be such that the integrals are finite. The fragmentary words around this note are illegible.

(3) Integration by parts (Green's theorem in Riemann's form). His Green formula is ∫(X_x + Y_y) dT = −∫(X ∂x/∂p + Y ∂y/∂p) ds. Here p is the inward normal and s the arc, with ∂x/∂p = ∂y/∂s and ∂y/∂p = −∂x/∂s.
- Pointwise identity [my fill]: (u_x − β_y)u'_x + (u_y + β_x)u'_y = div(u'∇u) − u'Δu + ∂_x(−β_y u') + ∂_y(β_x u').
- Integrating, the β-terms give a pure boundary term +∫u' ∂β/∂s ds. The u-terms give −∫u' ∂u/∂p ds − ∫u'Δu dT.
- Hence ∫[...] dT = −∫u'Δu dT − ∫(∂u/∂p − ∂β/∂s) u' ds.
This boundary term is the line '−∫(∂u/∂p − ∂β/∂s) u' ds', rewritten as '∫u'(∂u/∂p − ∂β/∂s) ds'.

(4) The last line forms ∫[(u_x − β_y)u'_x + (u_y + β_x)u'_y] dT + ∫(∂u/∂p − ∂β/∂s) u' ds. By (3) this equals −∫u'Δu dT [implicit, my fill; consistent with the next page]. The boundary integrals run over the boundaries of the pieces into which T is cut along discontinuity lines; on the outer boundary they vanish because u' = 0. The next page then argues:
- N = 0 for all such u' forces Δu = 0 in each piece.
- What remains is the weak 'natural boundary condition' along the discontinuity curves: ∫(∇u·∇u') dT + ∫(∂u/∂p) u' dF = 0. This is shown there for β = 0, the form appearing in the dissertation.
errors: No mathematical error on the page. The sign of the boundary term is correct with Riemann's convention (p inward normal, s oriented so that ∂x/∂p = ∂y/∂s, ∂y/∂p = −∂x/∂s). With an outward normal, both signs would flip.

Implicit unjustified step (as in the dissertation): the existence of a minimising u is tacitly assumed. The pencil argument at the top only shows that two minima/infima coincide, not that a minimiser exists. This is the gap later criticised by Weierstrass (1870).
Integration by parts presumes enough smoothness of u, β, u' on each piece. Riemann only requires finiteness of the Dirichlet-type integrals, so the step is formally rather than rigorously justified.

results.what: First variation of Ω(u) = ∫[(u_x − β_y)^2 + (u_y + β_x)^2] dT and its reduction via Green's theorem to −∫u'Δu dT − ∫(∂u/∂p − ∂β/∂s) u' ds
results.modern_name: Euler–Lagrange equation / weak formulation of the Laplace equation via the Dirichlet integral (Dirichlet principle), with natural boundary terms
results.usually_credited_to: Green (1828), Gauss (1839), Thomson (1847), Dirichlet (lectures); named 'Dirichlet principle' by Riemann himself (dissertation 1851, Abelsche Functionen 1857)

results.what: Uniqueness of the minimum: two minimal values cannot each be smaller than the other, hence equal; leads to uniqueness of the harmonic function with given boundary data and conditions at discontinuities
results.modern_name: Uniqueness part of the Dirichlet principle / uniqueness for the Dirichlet problem

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of the Dirichlet-principle section of Riemann's 1851 dissertation, with the same functional Ω, the same β-modified Dirichlet integral and the same Green-theorem convention. The content is well known as his; only the draft form is of archival interest.

transcription_corrections: 'b' throughout is almost certainly Riemann's β (the second given function, as in Dissertation §16), written in a form resembling b.
The area element 'dS' is probably 'dT' (Riemann's notation for the surface element of T); the boundary element is ds.
The lines '−∫(∂u/∂p − ∂b/∂s) u' ds' and the final '...u' ds' have a correction over the u' (a superscript, possibly a struck letter); the reading u' ds fits the mathematics.

Top pencil text: read roughly 'es ergiebt sich von diesen [Functionen] derselbe Ω; ... es kann [also] 𝔘 nicht < U_1, ebenso kann U_1 nicht < 𝔘, folglich 𝔘 = U_1'. Here 'kann nicht' is an interlinear correction replacing 'muss', and 'immer' is struck. The reading is uncertain.
'– ein gieße mit einem Werden – ?' is unreliable; the words are illegible fragments (possibly '... mit einem Worte ...').

The left-margin fragments ('=0,', dashes, 'ung', single letters) are line ends of the cut-off left half of the sheet, not independent content; '′ = 0' presumably completes 'u′ = 0' (u′ vanishing on the boundary).
